eyebrow: Quantum Programming with Q# & Azure Quantum · Chapter 6
subtitle: Lesson 23 · Q# vs. Qiskit: Comparative Project

steps.label: A Qiskit circuit is data you build and inspect
steps.sub: A Q# operation is itself the unit of computation

steps.label: The operation/function split buys compiler guarantees
steps.sub: Dynamic circuit objects don't give you that

steps.label: Dynamic circuit objects buy introspection and rewriting
steps.sub: A compiled, typed language doesn't give you that

steps.label: Both express the same algorithms
steps.sub: The difference is the programming model, not capability

code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.h(0)
qc.cx(0, 1)
qc.measure_all()

# qc is a real Python object: draw it, count its depth,
# transpile it, compose() it with another circuit
caption: Nothing about building the circuit requires running it — its existence as mutable, inspectable data is the point.

eyebrow: Q# — the operation is the computation
caption: What you get instead: compiler-enforced structure — the operation/function split and compiler-derived functors.

eyebrow: What each model actually buys you

steps.label: Qiskit's cost
steps.sub: Nothing guarantees a custom gate behaves correctly under .inverse() or .control() — that's on you

steps.label: Q#'s cost
steps.sub: You lose the ad hoc runtime circuit inspection and rewriting that falls out of an object model

steps.label: Qiskit fits circuit-manipulation work
steps.sub: Transpilation research, visual editors, programmatic composition at runtime

steps.label: Q# fits large, modular, team-maintained codebases
steps.sub: Where the compiler itself catches a class of bugs before anyone reviews the code

subtitle: Two tools answering genuinely different questions, for genuinely different hardware eras.
